text: ROS 2. Industry standard robotics middleware. DDS-based pub-sub, originally from the defense world. More mature than dora, way more drivers, way bigger community. The problem for LLM robotics is twofold. One: the wire format is CDR-serialized IDL messages, which means every inter-process hop is serialize plus deserialize, which means 4MB camera frames cost you every time. Dora's Arrow-plus-shared-memory path is genuinely 10-17x faster for the Python case, and the README cites benchmarks. Two: ROS 2's data model is fixed-schema IDL, which is friendly to C++ codegen and unfriendly to a Python planner node that wants to dump "a list of detected objects with arbitrary fields per detection" — Arrow is columnar and heterogeneous, which is what LLM tool-use outputs actually look like.

speaker: a
text: For LLM workloads, yes. For "I'm writing a 2015-era motion planner in C++ on an industrial arm," ROS 2 is still the right pick. Horses, courses. Zenoh. Not a competitor — it's a transport. Eclipse project, pub-sub plus storage plus queries. Dora uses Zenoh as its cross-machine data plane. You can run a Zenoh-only stack if you want, but then you're building coordinator, daemon, lifecycle, fault tolerance, CLI yourself. Dora is roughly "Zenoh plus a supervisor plus YAML plus Arrow plus a CLI." Durable workflows. Temporal, Restate, Inngest. Totally different model. Temporal persists every event to a log, lets workflows run for days or weeks across crashes, re-hydrates state by replaying history. The latency floor is tens of milliseconds minimum and often hundreds. That is the wrong SLA for a 100Hz control loop. But it is exactly the right SLA for an LLM planner that's thinking about "what should the robot do over the next twenty minutes" — durable, checkpointable, survives a coordinator restart. So you compose them. Dora handles perception-plus-control at the real-time layer, Temporal handles the long-horizon plan-revision layer, and the two talk via a dora node that subscribes to Temporal signals and emits goals onto a dora topic.
